issues.description: The template Farm.java defines singFarmSongVerse without the Animal parameter (commented out), but the problem statement and solution require singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal). This mismatch can confuse students and leads to signature changes beyond just implementing TODO bodies.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template method signature to `private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)` and add/import the Animal type (or include a commented stub with the correct signature) to match the UML and intended implementation.

issues.description: The template Main.java (commented example) calls `farm.feed()` but the problem statement and solution define the method as `feedAllAnimals()`. This inconsistency may mislead students into implementing the wrong method name or thinking both are required.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template Main.java example call from `farm.feed()` to `farm.feedAllAnimals()` to align with the required API.

issues.description: The method for feeding all animals is named inconsistently across artifacts: the problem statement requires Farm.feedAllAnimals(), the solution implements feedAllAnimals(), but the template Main (example usage) calls farm.feed(). This makes it unclear to students which identifier is expected for the same concept (feeding all animals).
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template Main.java example call from farm.feed() to farm.feedAllAnimals() (or, less preferably, rename the required method everywhere to feed()) so the same identifier is used consistently across statement, template, and solution.

issues.description: The Animal name setter is referred to generically as a 'setter' in the problem statement, but the solution uses setName(String newName) where the parameter is named newName instead of name. While minor, this can add friction when students mirror the described signature and compare with reference code or IDE suggestions.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the setter parameter naming with the most expected identifier by using setName(String name) (or clarify in the problem statement that parameter naming is flexible).
